refresh_policy.rationale: Apple Photos imports require the user to manually export files from Photos.app (File → Export → Export Unmodified Originals) into the import directory; there is no API or background-refreshable path — PhotoKit requires a signed app bundle and is not reachable from this connector, and the reverse-engineered Photos.sqlite path is out of scope by design.

streams.name: photos
streams.description: File-level metadata AND hydrated bytes for images and videos exported from Photos.app, within a configured size cap. Uses the same shared local-media blob hydration module as google_takeout's photos stream (src/local-media-blob-hydration.ts) — bounded local read, sha256 content hash, MIME-by-extension, and upload through the runtime's reference-blob-uploader when blob-upload bindings are configured. A record's `id` is derived from content_sha256 alone, so the same photo present in more than one Photos.app export collapses to one record rather than duplicating.

display.label: Your exported photos and videos
display.detail: Filename, size, content hash, MIME type, file-modified timestamp, and (within the size cap) hydrated bytes for each file found in the Photos.app export directory. hydration_status/hydration_error explain when bytes are absent (oversized or unreadable) without dropping the record. EXIF/XMP fields (taken date, GPS, camera) are present in the schema but not populated in this cut — a bounded, explicit omission, not silently missing coverage.

streams.name: coverage_diagnostics
streams.description: Safe coverage status for this connector's one known local store (the Photos.app export directory), so a local-collector run always leaves durable, honest coverage evidence even when the export directory is missing or empty — never a silent zero-evidence run.

display.label: Local collector coverage status
display.detail: Whether the Photos.app export directory was found and collected on this run.
